html:
The northern half of Sakhalin, a long island north of Japan, as it was under Russian rule in 1914. Japan held the south.

Sakhalin's first peoples were the Ainu in the south and the Nivkh and Orok in the north. Russia and Japan both claimed it until the Treaty of Saint Petersburg of 1875 gave the whole island to Russia in exchange for the Kuril Islands. Russia made it a penal colony; the writer Anton Chekhov visited in 1890 and described the convicts' misery in his book Sakhalin Island.

After the Russo-Japanese War, the Treaty of Portsmouth of 1905 split the island at the 50th parallel, and the south became Japanese Karafuto. Japan also occupied the north from 1920 to 1925, during the Russian Civil War. In August 1945 the Soviet army took the south, and the whole island has been Russian ever since, under the Soviet Union and then Russia.
sum: The northern half of Sakhalin, a long island north of Japan, as it was under Russian rule in 1914. Japan held the south.
